mechanic: Two narrators: each is certain of their own part of the evening, neither account answers the question alone, and the two are read as one timeline.
note: Spoilers. The logic written before the prose, in the shape sketched in docs/archipelago-plan.md. Here the two narrators' accounts are the clues, each already a unit with its own source; the frame is the first narrator's.

frame.says: Fifty pounds put in the study desk as the dinner gong went were gone when the guests had left.

questions.asks: Who took the notes from the study desk?

rules_out.Captain Voss: c.landing: he was watched all the time he was out
rules_out.George Marlow, the maid: c.table: they never left the dining-room
rules_out.anyone before the joint: c.landing: nobody else crossed the hall

clues.source: George Marlow, who did not leave the table
clues.says: He and the maid stayed in the dining-room throughout; Clara was upstairs from the soup until the joint; Captain Voss went out during the fish, Miss Pym during the dessert.

clues.source: Clara Marlow, on the nursery landing above the hall from the soup until the joint
clues.says: Captain Voss took something from his overcoat and went straight back, never out of her sight or near the study door; nobody else crossed the hall.
She went down as the joint was carried in, and after that nobody watched the hall.
